finding.title: Tighten bulk_prior_completion_b6_b8_test.dart's greaterThanOrEqualTo(2) assertion to an exact count

evidence.quote: 'Should have one active completion per curriculum for Berakhot 2',

finding.why: The test's own reason string states the invariant is exactly one active row per curriculum (2 curricula seeded => exactly 2), but the matcher accepts any count >= 2. A duplicate-insert regression in BulkPriorCompletionService.execute (e.g. a double-write bug) would silently pass this assertion, which is the 'assertion weaker than what the source can do wrong' pattern the audit is hunting for.
finding.recommendation: Replace greaterThanOrEqualTo(2) with equals(2) (or hasLength(2)) to match the stated invariant.
acceptance_criteria: Test 2 in the 'Finding 8' group asserts rows.length == 2 (or equivalent exact matcher), and fails if execute() is made to double-insert

finding.title: Delete or rewrite bulk_prior_completion_b6_b8_test.dart's stale AC3 test now that supersededAt was dropped

evidence.quote: // W3.29 dropped `supersededAt`. The helper still inserts 3 stages (2

finding.why: AC3 (lines 325-397) and its helper _seedStagesWithSuperseded (lines 216-239) were written to prove superseded stages are excluded from bulk-mark-prior. W3.29 removed the supersededAt column entirely, so the helper can no longer create a 'superseded' row, and the test's own comment admits 'the only 2 active expectation was outdated' — it now just re-proves AC1's '3 stages => 3 completions' with extra indirection. The test still reads as coverage for supersession filtering to anyone skimming the group, which is misleading, and the dead helper is pure maintenance cost.
finding.recommendation: Remove AC3 and _seedStagesWithSuperseded (their coverage is already fully subsumed by AC1), or repurpose the test name/comment to state plainly it is a duplicate-of-AC1 regression check for the schema migration itself.
acceptance_criteria: no test or helper in this file references a superseded-stage scenario that the current schema (no supersededAt column) cannot represent

finding.title: Assert the actual curriculum chip, not generic Container count, in tracks_studydays_and_content_hierarchy_l1_test.dart test #20
finding.why: Test #20 is named 'curriculum chip visible in breadcrumb area' but only checks that at least one Container widget exists anywhere on screen. Any full Scaffold/AppBar-based screen contains multiple unrelated Containers, so this assertion is true regardless of whether _RootCurriculumChip (the widget it claims to test, which wraps CurriculumLabel.curriculum(...) in a Container) renders at all — if the chip were deleted entirely the test would still pass.
finding.recommendation: Assert on the chip specifically, e.g. find.byKey(const Key('content_hierarchy_root_chip')) when interactive, or find.byType(CurriculumLabel) / the rendered curriculum text, instead of find.byType(Container).
acceptance_criteria: test #20 fails if _RootCurriculumChip is removed from the widget tree (verified by temporarily deleting it and observing red)

finding.title: Register onDispose when overriding userDatabaseProvider with inMemoryDb() in tracks_studydays_and_content_hierarchy_l1_test.dart

evidence.quote: /// Callers MUST `await db.close()` in `tearDown` to free the native

finding.why: The production userDatabaseProvider registers ref.onDispose(database.close) so the DB is closed when its ProviderScope is torn down; overriding the provider with a bare `(ref) => inMemoryDb()` replaces that entire body and drops the dispose registration, so none of the 4 fresh NativeDatabase.memory() instances created by this file's 27 widget tests are ever closed — a direct violation of drift_memory.dart's documented 'Callers MUST await db.close()' contract and a native-resource leak that scales with every widget test using this override pattern.
finding.recommendation: Add `ref.onDispose(db.close)` inside each override lambda (e.g. `userDatabaseProvider.overrideWith((ref) { final db = inMemoryDb(); ref.onDispose(db.close); return db; })`), or capture the db per-test and close it in the test's teardown.
acceptance_criteria: every userDatabaseProvider.overrideWith((ref) => inMemoryDb()) call site in this file registers a matching close via ref.onDispose or explicit teardown

finding.title: Split the 5 oversized hand-written test files in batch t1-test-cross-p5 below the 400-line AG-3 cap
finding.why: All 5 exceed AG-3's 400-line hand-written-file cap by 2.4x-3.5x, well past the digest's own '401-line file' minimal example. In bulk_prior_completion_b6_b8_test.dart a concrete driver is visible: BulkPriorCompletionService + CompletionRepositoryImpl are hand-constructed with near-identical arguments roughly 10 separate times (e.g. lines 279-299, 351-369, 412-430, 482-491, 541-552...) instead of one shared builder — a Fowler Extract-Method opportunity that alone would meaningfully shrink the file. Large files raise merge-conflict odds, slow comprehension/navigation for both humans and agents, and make it harder to run/inspect a single scenario in isolation.
finding.recommendation: Split each file along its existing group()/journey boundaries (e.g. one file per E2E-#### journey, one per L1 coverage letter-group, one per Bug-ID), and factor repeated service/repository construction in bulk_prior_completion_b6_b8_test.dart into a single `_buildHarness(...)` helper.
acceptance_criteria: AG-3 checker (once implemented) reports 0 violators among this batch's files, or each split file is individually ≤400 hand-written lines
